edges.description: Neuronal loss in CA4 within the sclerotic hippocampus triggers aberrant collateral sprouting of dentate granule cell mossy fibers into the dentate granule cell layer.
Subfield neuronal loss and reorganization in CA1 disrupt the trisynaptic pathway and produce subicular disinhibition and synchronized spontaneous excitability.
Structural injury and gliotic remodeling in the sclerotic hippocampus can drive broader extrahippocampal hub reorganization in MTLE-HS.
Subfield neuronal depletion and astrogliosis manifest radiologically as hippocampal subfield and whole-hippocampal volume loss on MRI.
Progressive hippocampal damage and synaptic reorganization underlie pharmacoresistance to anti-seizure medications in MTLE-HS.
Recurrent excitatory mossy-fiber collaterals amplify dentate granule cell and downstream hippocampal circuit hyperexcitability in proportion to the extent of sprouting.
Recurrent hippocampal circuit hyperexcitability recruits and remodels distributed limbic and cortical hubs.
Synchronized hyperexcitability in the sclerotic mesial temporal circuits initiates focal mesial temporal seizures.
Localized ictal discharges arising in hyperexcitable mesial temporal limbic circuits produce characteristic epigastric, autonomic, and experiential auras with preserved awareness.
Recruitment of mesial temporal limbic circuits during ictal propagation produces oroalimentary and manual automatisms with impaired awareness.
Reorganized hippocampal and extrahippocampal limbic-cortical hubs participate in the distributed epileptic network of MTLE-HS.
Functional network disruption beyond local hippocampal subfield atrophy is implicated in verbal memory impairment in MTLE-HS.

evidence.reference_title: Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis
evidence.snippet: Typical seizures consist of a characteristic aura that is frequently a rising epigastric sensation associated with emotional disturbances, illusions, and autonomic symptoms (widened pupils, palpitations), progressive impairment of consciousness, oro-alimentary automatisms (lip smacking, chewing, licking, tooth grinding), behavioral arrest, head deviation, dystonic postures, hand and verbal automatisms.
